title: MicroResponse Profiles — Compact Mode brainstorm
body:
Quick note / rough PRD + parking lot for a lightweight feature that lets clients request extremely compact, fidelity-aware responses. This is a personal scratchpad — lots of open questions.

Context / Motivation:
- Problem: many consumer and mobile use cases need short, immediate answers (notifications, inline suggestions, search snippets, system messages) where long exposition is wasteful and expensive.
- Existing levers (max_tokens, temperature, instruct templates) are too blunt: they either cut valuable content or still produce verbose outputs that drive token costs and latency.
- Goal: provide a first-class, server-side "compact" output mode that optimizes model prompting, sampling, and post-processing to produce tiny, useful responses with explicit fidelity hints and an easy path to expand if the client wants more.

Primary idea (high-level):
- Offer a Response Profile API param: response_profile = one of ["micro", "concise", "balanced", "expanded"]
- "micro" is the extreme compact mode: aggressive compression, prioritized facts only, single-sentence or fragment outputs, token budget ~8-48 depending on model.
- Responses include a small metadata header (machine-only) with a fidelity_hint (low/medium) and an expand_token_cursor (opaque) so clients can request a follow-up "expand" call that keeps context and cheaply generates more detail.

User stories / personas:
- Mobile news app: show 1-line digest in push or headline card. If user taps, client calls expand to see full summary. Saves tokens across billions of impressions.
- Chatbot on ecommerce site: show fast "short answer" for product Qs; escalate to detailed explanation only on click.
- Internal tool snack responses: ephemeral quick suggestions for engineers where verbosity is distracting.

Behavioral ideas / runtime levers (what engine should do):
- Prompting: specialized micro-prompt templates that prioritize key facts and avoid preambles. Possibly include example-based instructs: "Respond in 10 words or less, no qualifiers."
- Sampling: use nucleus or top-p with lower entropy to avoid long tails.
- Post-processing: automatic truncation with grammar heuristics; optional compressed summaries (sentence compression).
- Token budgeting: platform enforces a soft token cap and returns a cost_estimate in response metadata.
- Expand flow: a compact response returns an expand_cursor token (opaque id) referencing cached KV context; an expand API call continues generation without re-rendering whole context — cheaper and lower latency.

API sketch (very rough):
- request: POST /v1/generate { prompt: ..., model: ..., response_profile: "micro", verbosity_hint: "low", max_profile_tokens: 32, allow_expand: true }
- response: { text: "Short answer...", profile: "micro", fidelity_hint: "low", expand_cursor: "cXJ...", tokens_used: "19" }

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Developers can opt-in with response_profile param.
- "micro" responses average < 40 tokens on our curated test prompts (50% of intents), while maintaining >= 85% correctness on binary QA checks for those intents.
- Expand API returns an additional chunk with < 150 additional tokens and latency < baseline full response.
- Telemetry surfaced in Console: per-profile token cost, latency, and quality delta vs baseline.

Success metrics (initial):
- 30% reduction in avg tokens for mobile app vertical for customers who adopt profile in first 60 days.
- Expand usage < 10% of micro responses (i.e., most micro answers suffice).
- No significant drop in NPS for clients using micro profile for supported flows.

Design / UX thoughts (client):
- UI shows chevron/ellipsis indicating expandable content. Tapping triggers expand API and shows spinner then full content.
- Provide developer docs with UX patterns and recommended default thresholds by vertical (search, chat, mobile).

Operational considerations / infra:
- Need cheap caching of compact responses and small expand cursors — consider ephemerally pinning KV cache for 5 minutes per expand_cursor to keep expand latency low.
- Fallback rules: if expand_cursor expired, expand triggers full re-generation (higher cost). Provide explicit status in response.
- Rate limiting: protect expand endpoint to avoid abuse (clients might repeatedly expand).

Open questions / risks (parking lot):
- How to guarantee legal/compliance metadata flows if content is compressed and we drop source attribution? Risk: removing critical provenance when summarizing.
- UX: when micro answer is wrong, users might trust it because it’s concise. Need a confidence signal or way to show uncertainty.
- Cost vs quality tradeoff: how to recommend defaults per model and vertical?
- Expand semantics: is expand a continuation (keeps micro as a prefix) or a regeneration with broader context? Continuation easier for latency but may repeat.
- How to price? micro could be priced lower per token (but expansion costs add complexity).

Short experiments to run (low-effort explorations):
1) Internal eval harness: run 500 prompts across 4 verticals (FAQ, search snippet, product QA, quick tasks) comparing baseline vs micro prompts. Measure token counts, answer correctness (binary), and user-perceived helpfulness via quick internal rating.
2) Prototype expand_cursor via short-lived KV store: generate micro responses with pointer; measure expand latency and extra tokens.
3) UX prototype in a sample mobile app (one feature flag) with analytics for expand rate and CTR.

Next steps (action items):
- Run quick eval (owner: Imogen) by 2026-03-17.
- Sync with serving-runtime to check feasibility of short-lived KV for expand cursors (owner: Riley) by 2026-03-12.
- Mock API spec and add to developer quickstart (owner: Maya) — stub docs and examples.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider adding a small "source_hint" token (e.g., "s1") that maps to provenance list returned separately to save bytes.
- Might integrate with Optimize: recommend micro profile when cost per session exceeds threshold.
- Evaluate overlap with existing session-compression features — ensure complementary, not duplicated.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy if we pursue further.
